description: AWS Application Load Balancer telemetry from the AWS/ApplicationELB CloudWatch namespace (RED method, then saturation and limits): load balancer, LCU, target, and target group health metrics.

panels.description: Requests where a target was chosen, per load balancer and per zone. Rejected requests are not counted here. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Requests ($period)

panels.description: Concurrent and new TCP connections, clients to load balancer and load balancer to targets. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Connections ($period)

panels.description: Bytes processed over IPv4 and IPv6, headers and payload, both directions. One LCU dimension. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Processed bytes ($period)

panels.description: Listener rules evaluated while routing, default rule excluded. One LCU dimension. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Rule evaluations ($period)

panels.description: Responses the load balancer answered itself: redirects and fixed responses. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Load balancer actions ($period)

panels.description: Connections rejected because the load balancer reached its maximum number of connections. The limit scales with the load balancer; any value is saturation. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Rejected connections ($period)

panels.description: 4XX and 5XX generated by the load balancer, not by targets. 4XX means a malformed or incomplete request; 5XX is detailed in the next panel. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Load balancer HTTP errors ($period)

panels.description: 502: target closed the connection or sent a malformed response. 503: no healthy target. 504: target did not answer within the idle timeout. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Load balancer 5XX by code ($period)

panels.description: Requests outside RFC 7230 and requests with invalid header fields, dropped or forwarded according to the routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields attribute. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#load-balancer-metric-table
panels.title: Malformed requests ($period)

panels.description: Load balancer capacity units billed per hour: the highest of new connections, active connections, processed bytes, and rule evaluations. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#lcu-metric-table https://aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/pricing/
panels.title: Consumed LCUs ($period)

panels.description: Share of the load balancer's current capacity in use. A hundred during a spike means demand outran automatic scaling; sustained high values call for an LCU reservation. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#lcu-metric-table
panels.title: Capacity utilization ($period)

panels.description: Requests routed to the selected target groups. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Target group requests ($period)

panels.description: Average requests per healthy target of the group. The only valid statistic is Sum, which here is an average. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Requests per target ($period)

panels.description: Successful and redirect responses generated by the targets. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Target responses ($period)

panels.description: 4XX and 5XX generated by the targets, not by the load balancer. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Target HTTP errors ($period)

panels.description: Connections from the load balancer to a target that failed to establish, health checks excluded. Pods restarting, a wrong port, or a security group. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Target connection errors ($period)

panels.description: Time from the request leaving the load balancer to the first response header from the target, the target_processing_time of the access logs. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#metric-statistics
panels.title: Target response time ($period)

panels.description: Healthy targets as the Minimum across load balancer nodes, the statistic AWS recommends for alarms, unhealthy targets as the Maximum, and the floor from the min_healthy_targets variable. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#metric-statistics
panels.title: Target health ($period)

panels.description: Targets flagged by anomaly detection, targets under automatic mitigation, and targets disabled by a zonal shift. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-metric-table
panels.title: Anomalous and mitigated targets ($period)

panels.description: Zones meeting the DNS and routing healthy-state thresholds of the target group. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html#target-group-health
panels.title: Healthy zones ($period)

panels.description: Zones marked unhealthy in DNS, and zones where the load balancer fails open to every target. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html#target-group-health
panels.title: Unhealthy zones ($period)

panels.description: Requests routed by the failover action to targets including unhealthy ones. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html#target-group-health-metric-table
panels.title: Fail-open requests ($period)

list.description: Floor for healthy targets, drawn on the Target health panel. Set it to the minimum replica count of the deployment.
list.label: min_healthy_targets
list.name: min_healthy_targets

title: AWS ALB CloudWatch
